{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sd-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"38f6080003a24af49b92c64aafc8af0662bfdb853517fa20a9f8396570c59dbe","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sd-class-std:lineage:23","source_registry_sha256":"a4e51960bfe4da242ea11046073ac8d3d0353ce120a5409a11c1f9ab4c4da57a","source_liveness_sha256":"1aea607665fc1312b9a6988c94545b32e414886d6d428b2b6d66e4261f9397f1"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Vehicle inspection, seating and mirrors","heading":"C — Knowledge dossier: Vehicle inspection, seating and mirrors","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Knowledge dossier: Vehicle inspection, seating and mirrors

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A23
Drivers can improve safety before moving by checking the vehicle, setting the seat and mirrors, fastening restraints, clearing the view and securing carried items. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A23
Underinflated, overinflated or low-tread tires can create road-safety problems. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A23
The handbook recommends checking tire pressure with a gauge every month. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A23
Use the tire-pressure recommendation on the door-jamb sticker and check pressure while the tires are cold. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A23
Release air when measured tire pressure exceeds the vehicle recommendation and add air when it is below that recommendation. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A23
For the handbook’s tread check, hold a penny by Lincoln’s body and put his head first into the groove that appears deepest. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A23
Seeing Lincoln’s whole head in the handbook’s penny test means the tire is too worn to drive on and should be replaced. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A23
A driver must ensure that the vehicle being driven is safe to operate. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A23
A poorly maintained vehicle can break down, cause a crash or leave fewer options in an emergency. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A23
Follow the owner’s manual for routine maintenance, using a qualified mechanic for work that requires one. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A23
Have a mechanic inspect brakes that work poorly, make unusual noise or smells, or have a pedal that sinks to the floor. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A23
Check turn signals, brake lights, taillights and headlights from outside the vehicle to ensure that they work. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A23
Brake lights communicate stopping, while turn signals communicate a turn. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A23
Misaligned headlights may fail to light the useful area and may dazzle other drivers. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A23
Ask a mechanic to check headlights when night visibility is poor or other drivers repeatedly flash their headlights at you. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A24
Replace a damaged windshield because damaged glass may break more readily in a minor crash or after an impact. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A24
Keep all installed windshield, rear-window and headlight wipers working, and replace blades that do not clear water effectively. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A24
Worn or bald tires can lengthen stopping distance and make wet-road turning harder. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A24
Poor tire balance or low pressure can increase wear, reduce fuel economy and make steering or stopping more difficult. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A24
Have a mechanic investigate excessive bouncing, a shaking steering wheel or pulling to one side. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A24
Worn tires increase the risk of hydroplaning and of a flat tire. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A24
The recommended tire pressure in pounds per square inch is found in the owner’s manual or driver-side door jamb and should be checked with a gauge before entering the vehicle. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A24
The second penny-test description calls for replacing a tire when its tread does not reach at least Lincoln’s head with the coin inserted head first. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A24
Hard steering or a delayed response when the steering wheel is first turned requires a mechanic’s steering-system inspection. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A24
The suspension helps the driver control the vehicle and smooths the ride over different road surfaces. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A24
Repeated bouncing after a bump or stop, or difficulty controlling the vehicle, can mean the suspension needs a mechanic’s attention. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A24
The exhaust system reduces engine noise, cools exhaust gases and directs them toward the rear of the vehicle. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A24
A leaking exhaust can quickly expose vehicle occupants to lethal gases. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A24
Never run a vehicle engine in a closed garage. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A24
When sitting in a vehicle with the engine running for an extended time, open a window. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A24
Have the exhaust checked periodically because many exhaust leaks cannot be heard. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A24
A poorly running engine may lose needed power, fail to start or stall, waste fuel and pollute, so follow the owner’s maintenance procedures. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0024]

Misconceptions: A functioning light can still be misaligned; an air bag does not replace the seatbelt; tire pressure is checked against the vehicle recommendation rather than an invented universal value.
Mnemonics: Use tires, controls, view, position and belt as an authored preparation cue.
Glossary: Tread is the grooved tire surface; the suspension supports vehicle control and ride; a head restraint is positioned against the back of the head; blind spots are areas outside the mirror view.
Dynamic facts: Manufacturer-specific pressure and maintenance schedules come from the applicable vehicle documents. No model-specific value is invented; legal tint rules remain edition-bound.
